scenario: 你时间有限，需要决定 ML system design 备考精力主要投在生产落地技能还是理论证明。
scenario_en: You have limited prep time and need to choose between production ML system skills and theory proofs.
q: 该优先打磨哪种能力？
q_en: Which skill should you prioritize?
options: 深入啃 ML 理论推导和数学证明
打磨设计和落地生产 ML 系统的实践能力
长期死磕 Kaggle 排行榜刷分技巧，不练设计表达
全部依赖过往项目经验，不额外准备
options_en: Dive deep into ML theory and mathematical proofs.
Practice designing and shipping production ML systems.
Stay fixated on Kaggle leaderboard tuning instead of practicing design delivery.
Rely entirely on past experience with no targeted prep.
why: 指南本身定位是实践导向：不讲 ML 理论证明，聚焦在生产系统设计和面试表达上的技能。
why_en: The guide is deliberately practical, so your prep time is best spent on production ML system design and interview delivery, not theory proofs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个以数据科学和机器学习竞赛闻名的在线平台。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kaggle is an online platform known for data science and machine learning competitions.

optionExplanations: 数学证明适合偏研究的面试，但这份指南不考证明，投入这块和目标考察点错位。
这正是指南主线——面试考的是设计判断，不是公式推导。
死磕排行榜刷分练的是调参手感，和系统设计要展示的取舍推理几乎不重叠。
公司预期差异很大，裸考等于把范围不确定性留到考场上才发现。
optionExplanations_en: Math proofs suit research interviews, but this guide skips proofs entirely, so that effort is misdirected.
This lines up with what the interview actually tests: design judgment, not derivations.
Grinding leaderboard scores hones tuning instincts, which barely overlaps with the tradeoff reasoning system design wants.
Company expectations vary widely, so skipping prep leaves that gap unresolved until interview day.

scenario: "ML Engineer" 这个头衔在业界定义不统一，不同公司对同一头衔的期待差别很大。
scenario_en: The title "ML Engineer" is not standardized, and companies use the same title for very different expectations.
q: 这直接导致备考出现什么问题？
q_en: What prep problem does this create?
options: 所有公司的面试题目和考察重点完全相同，没有差异
面试风格和考察重点因公司差异很大，难以判断该准备什么
完全不考数据、模型这些技术判断，只看谈吐是否流利、表达是否自信
候选人可以跳过所有准备，临场发挥就足够
options_en: Every company's questions and focus areas are exactly the same, with no differences.
Interview style and focus vary a lot by company, making it hard to know what to prepare.
The interview never tests data or model judgment at all, only how confident and fluent you sound.
Candidates can skip all preparation and just wing it on the spot.
why: 岗位定义不统一是根因：同一头衔在不同公司可能侧重应用、基础设施或研究，备考前必须先弄清楚考察方向。
why_en: Because the ML engineer role is not standardized, interview focus varies a lot by company, so you need to know the target before you prepare.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责把机器学习模型落地为生产系统的工程师岗位，各公司定义不统一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ML engineer is an engineering role that ships machine learning into production, and its scope varies widely by company.

optionExplanations: 如果真是这样，头衔差异就不会造成任何备考困扰，但现实里同一头衔在不同公司考法差很多。
头衔越模糊，公司间的考法差异就越大，这正是备考前要先确认方向的原因。
系统设计面试仍然会深挖数据、模型和上线这些技术判断，不会只靠谈吐和自信程度打分。
临场发挥赌的是运气，公司对同一头衔的预期差异恰恰会让你答偏方向。
optionExplanations_en: If this were true, the title mismatch wouldn't create any confusion, but in reality the same title tests very different things.
The vaguer the title, the more interview focus diverges across companies, which is exactly why you need to pin down the target first.
System design interviews still dig into data, model, and launch judgment, not just how confident you sound.
Winging it bets on luck, and companies' differing expectations for the same title make that gamble worse.

scenario: 你不确定某家公司 ML 面试偏应用型设计还是基础设施方向。
scenario_en: You are not sure whether a company's ML interview leans toward applied design or infrastructure.
q: 最应该在什么时候和 recruiter 澄清范围？
q_en: When should you clarify the scope with the recruiter?
options: 设计正讲到一半，才突然打断面试官追问范围细节
面试开场先说自己没把握、自我贬低
面试前主动找 recruiter 谈清角色范围
全程什么都不问，等分数打出来后才追问范围
options_en: Interrupt mid-design to suddenly ask about scope details.
Open the interview by talking yourself down.
Talk to the recruiter about the role and scope beforehand.
Stay silent the whole time and only ask after your score is already in.
why: 角色期待应该在面试前确认；面试中途打断或用不确定性自我设限都会削弱信号。
why_en: Clarify interview scope with the recruiter before the interview, not by interrupting mid-interview or undermining yourself at the start.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试中确实出现范围模糊，仍可以简短确认题目边界，但不要用整体不确定性给自己贴标签。
tradeoff: 面试前用一次沟通换清晰范围 vs 面试中用自我贬低换心理安全感

termDefinitions.meaning: 招聘方的招聘协调人，通常负责面试流程和岗位信息沟通。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A recruiter is the hiring-side contact who coordinates the interview process and can share role expectations.

optionExplanations: 临时打断会打乱作答节奏，而且这时候再调整复习方向已经来不及了。
开场自我贬低是在面试官还没评估你之前，先替自己扣分。
拿到范围后能针对性分配复习时间，还不会影响临场表现。
等分数已经打出来才问，澄清对这一轮已经没有意义。
optionExplanations_en: Interrupting mid-design breaks your flow, and by then it's too late to adjust what you studied.
Opening with self-doubt docks your score before the interviewer has even started assessing you.
Getting scope early lets you target your prep without costing you anything during the interview.
Asking after your score is already in means the clarification can't help this attempt.

q: ML 岗 loop 里，四轮技术面分别对应哪几类 ML 面试？（多选）
q_en: In an ML loop, which four ML interview types do the technical rounds map to? (Select all)
options: Applied ML System Design
ML Infra Design
AI/ML Research
AI/ML Research Engineering
options_en: Applied ML System Design, designing production ML solutions for business problems.
ML Infra Design, building the platforms that serve and train models.
AI or ML Research, inventing or improving algorithms.
AI or ML Research Engineering, implementing and optimizing research code.
why: 四种面试类型考察点不同——业务落地、基础设施、理论研究、论文实现；本指南主线是 Applied ML System Design。
why_en: The four ML interview types test different things — business-to-ML translation, infrastructure, theory research, and paper implementation — and this guide's primary focus is applied ML system design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向业务问题设计可落地生产机器学习系统的面试类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Applied ML System Design is an interview type about designing production ML systems for a business problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 聚焦模型服务、训练平台等机器学习基础设施的面试类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ML Infra Design is an interview type about building the platforms that serve and train ML models.

termDefinitions.meaning: 聚焦理论创新和前沿算法的面试类型，多用于研究科学家岗位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI/ML Research is an interview type focused on theory and novel algorithms, common for research scientist roles.

termDefinitions.meaning: 连接研究和软件工程，聚焦论文实现与性能优化的面试类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Research Engineering is an interview type focused on implementing and optimizing research code.

optionExplanations: 把业务问题转成能上线的生产方案，这条路径是这份指南展开的主线。
ML Infra Design 考的是训练、serving、特征库这类支撑多个模型的平台能力，不针对单个业务模型。
AI/ML Research 考的是提出或改进算法本身，常见于研究科学家岗位。
Research Engineering 考的是把论文思路实现成能跑、能验证的代码和实验。
optionExplanations_en: It turns a business problem into a shippable production solution, the path this guide centers on.
ML Infra Design is about platform work like training, serving, and feature stores that support many models, not one business model.
AI/ML Research is about proposing or improving the algorithms themselves, common for research scientist roles.
Research Engineering is about turning a paper's idea into runnable, verifiable code and experiments.
scenario: 你拿到 ML 岗 loop 日程：四轮技术面分别由业务、平台、研究、研究工程团队出题，要分开准备。
scenario_en: Your ML loop has four technical rounds, each run by a different team — product, platform, research, and research engineering — so you have to prep them separately.

q: Applied ML System Design 面试主要评估候选人什么能力？
q_en: What does an Applied ML System Design interview mainly assess?
options: 证明一个全新的优化算法
手写 GPU kernel 提升训练速度
背出模型发布的具体年份
把业务问题转成可落地的生产 ML 方案
options_en: Prove a brand-new optimization algorithm.
Hand-write GPU kernels to speed up training.
Recite the exact release year of a model.
Translate a business problem into a production-ready ML solution.
why: Applied ML SD 面试默认已有常规 ML 基础设施，重点考数据、模型选择、部署和监控这条业务到生产的链路。
why_en: Applied ML system design interviews assess turning a business problem into a production ML solution, assuming standard ML infrastructure is already available.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Business[Business problem] --> Objective[ML objective]
  Objective --> Data[Data labels]
  Data --> Model[Model choice]
  Model --> Production[Deploy evaluate]

termDefinitions.meaning: 运行在 GPU 上的底层计算函数，通常用于加速训练或推理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GPU kernel is a low-level function that runs on the GPU, typically used to speed up training or inference.

optionExplanations: 证明新算法属于研究面试的考点，应用型设计默认基础设施已就绪，不会现场证明算法。
GPU kernel 调优是底层性能工程，通常划进 infra 或研究岗，不是应用设计的主线。
背版本年份是纯记忆，和数据、模型、上线这条设计判断链没有关系。
这正是应用型设计的核心——把业务目标一路走到能上线的生产方案。
optionExplanations_en: Proving a new algorithm belongs to research interviews; applied design assumes standard infra is already there, no live proofs needed.
GPU kernel tuning is low-level performance work that usually falls under infra or research, not the applied-design main track.
Reciting a release year is pure recall and has nothing to do with the data-to-model-to-launch judgment chain.
This is exactly the applied-design core: carry a business goal all the way to a shippable production solution.
scenario: 你面推荐团队的 Applied ML SD 轮，公司已有成熟的训练平台和 serving，不需要你自己搭。
scenario_en: You are in the applied ML system design round for a recommendations team, where the training platform and serving stack already exist and you do not build them.

scenario: 题目是「设计社交平台的有害内容检测系统」。
scenario_en: The prompt is: design a harmful-content detection system for a social platform.
q: 这属于哪类 ML 面试的典型题？
q_en: Which ML interview type is this?
options: AI/ML Research
Applied ML System Design
Research Engineering
普通电商网页产品的前端交互动效与视觉排版设计
options_en: AI/ML Research.
Applied ML System Design.
Research Engineering.
Front-end interaction motion and visual layout design for an ordinary e-commerce web product.
why: 题目要求围绕数据、模型、审核动作、评估和生产约束展开，属于把业务问题落地成 ML 方案的应用型设计。
why_en: Harmful-content detection asks you to design data, model, moderation actions, and evaluation for production, which is a classic applied ML system design problem.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目改成设计分布式特征库或训练平台，就转向了 ML Infra Design。
tradeoff: 业务到生产的 ML 方案设计 vs 底层基础设施设计

termDefinitions.meaning: 检测并处理平台上有害或违规内容的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Content moderation is the system that detects and handles harmful or policy-violating content on a platform.

optionExplanations: 题目没有要求提出新算法或做理论证明，不是研究轮的考法。
题目给了明确的数据、模型判断和上线约束，正好落在应用型设计里。
题目不涉及复现论文或跑 benchmark，不是研究工程的考点。
内容审核的核心是模型怎么判断有害内容，不是页面元素怎么排版和交互。
optionExplanations_en: The prompt never asks for a new algorithm or theoretical proof, so it's not a research-round question.
The prompt gives concrete data, model judgment, and launch constraints, which is exactly applied design territory.
There's no paper to reproduce or benchmark to run here, so it doesn't fit research engineering.
Content moderation hinges on how the model judges harmful content, not on how page elements are laid out or interacted with.

q: ML Infra Design 面试更偏关注哪些内容？
q_en: What does an ML Infra Design interview focus on?
options: 具体某条内容审核政策的标签定义
怎么设计用户调研问卷和产品落地页文案措辞
模型服务、训练平台、特征库、管道和版本管理
人工标注团队的招聘、排班和绩效考核流程
options_en: The exact label definitions for one moderation policy.
How to design user research surveys and product landing-page copy wording.
Model serving, training platforms, feature stores, pipelines, and versioning.
The hiring, scheduling, and performance-review process for a labeling team.
why: Infra 面试关注可扩展、可靠、低成本的 ML 基础设施，不是单个业务模型的特征和 objective。
why_en: ML infrastructure interviews focus on scalable, reliable, low-cost platforms for serving, training, feature stores, and versioning, not one business model's features.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Infra[ML infra] --> Serving[Serving]
  Infra --> Training[Training]
  Infra --> Features[Feature store]
  Infra --> Versions[Versioning]

termDefinitions.meaning: 集中存储和管理特征数据，供训练和线上服务复用的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store is a system that centrally stores and serves feature data for both training and online serving.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把训练好的模型部署成可被请求调用的在线服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model serving deploys a trained model as an online service that can respond to requests.

optionExplanations: 标签定义属于某个具体业务模型的数据设计，是应用型面试的范畴。
问卷设计和文案措辞属于用户研究工作，和平台的可扩展性、可靠性完全不相关。
这正是 infra 面试反复考的几块能力——支撑多个模型的平台本身。
招聘、排班这类团队管理话题，跟系统本身怎么搭建没关系。
optionExplanations_en: Label definitions belong to one specific business model's data design, which is applied-interview territory.
Survey design and copy wording are user-research work, unrelated to whether a platform scales or stays reliable.
This is exactly what infra interviews keep testing — the platform that supports many models, not one.
Hiring and scheduling are team-management topics, unrelated to how the system itself is built.
scenario: 同一家公司另一轮由 ML Platform 团队出题：要支撑 50+ 个模型共用训练、上线和特征。
scenario_en: Another round at the same company is run by the ML platform team, which supports 50-plus models sharing training, serving, and features.

scenario: 题目是「设计一个每秒能处理百万请求的模型 serving 平台」。
scenario_en: The prompt is: design a model-serving platform that can handle one million requests per second.
q: 这更偏向哪类 ML 面试？
q_en: Which ML interview type does this lean toward?
options: ML Infra Design
内容分类这类 Applied ML System Design
AI/ML Research
纯产品增长 case
options_en: ML Infra Design.
Applied ML System Design, like a content classifier.
AI/ML Research.
A pure product-growth case.
why: 核心挑战是高吞吐、低延迟、扩缩容、版本管理和可靠性，这些是基础设施问题而不是单个模型的数据/特征问题。
why_en: The core challenge here is throughput, latency, scaling, versioning, and reliability, which makes this an ML infrastructure problem, not a single-model data problem.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目改成为某业务选标签、特征和模型，就回到 Applied ML System Design。
tradeoff: 服务规模和可靠性设计 vs 单个业务模型的数据/特征设计

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模型部署为在线服务、处理大量请求的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A serving platform deploys a model as an online service that handles a high volume of requests.

optionExplanations: 百万级 QPS、扩缩容和可靠性正是 infra 面试要考的那类平台挑战。
题目没给具体业务标签或数据，不是在考单个分类模型的设计。
题目没有要求提出新算法，不是理论创新轮。
题目关心的是服务能撑多大流量，跟增长指标毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: Million-QPS throughput, autoscaling, and reliability are exactly the platform challenges infra interviews test.
There's no concrete business label or dataset here, so it isn't testing a single classification model.
The prompt never asks for a new algorithm, so it isn't a theory-innovation round.
The prompt cares about how much traffic the service can hold, unrelated to growth metrics.

scenario: 同一个候选人分别拿到 AI/ML Research 和 Applied ML System Design 两种面试邀约。
scenario_en: The same candidate gets interview invitations for both AI/ML Research and Applied ML System Design.
q: 两者的主要差异是什么？
q_en: What is the main difference between the two?
options: 两者考察内容完全一样，公司之间也没有区别
研究类看重理论创新和 SOTA，应用类看重落地生产
应用类面试完全不需要任何数学推导、统计或建模基础知识
研究类面试只会问数据库表设计和索引优化这类实现问题
options_en: The two test exactly the same things, with no difference between companies.
Research values theoretical novelty and SOTA; applied values shipping to production.
Applied-track interviews need no math derivation, statistics, or modeling foundation at all, ever.
Research-track interviews only ever ask about database table design and index tuning.
why: Research 面试评估提出或改进算法的能力；Applied 面试评估把已知技术转化成生产系统的能力。
why_en: AI/ML research interviews assess proposing or improving algorithms, while applied interviews assess turning known techniques into a production system.
tradeoff: 理论创新与 SOTA 深度 vs 生产落地与业务转化能力

termDefinitions.meaning: state-of-the-art 的缩写，指某任务当前最好的已知方法或结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOTA stands for state-of-the-art, the best known method or result for a given task.

optionExplanations: 如果两者真的一样，同一候选人拿到两种邀约时表现就不该有差别，但实际差别很大。
这道题的关键分工：一个测你能不能造出新方法，另一个测你能不能把方案稳稳地扛上线。
应用型面试确实更少考数学证明，但基本的建模统计功底还是需要的。
研究面试实际考的是深度学习架构和优化理论，不是表设计和索引调优。
optionExplanations_en: If that were true, the same candidate wouldn't perform differently across the two invite types, but they clearly do.
The real split here is whether you can invent new methods versus whether you can ship known techniques reliably.
Applied interviews skip formal proofs, but you still need basic modeling statistics to reason about tradeoffs.
Research interviews actually dig into architecture and optimization theory, not schema design and index tuning.

q: Research Engineering 面试通常关注什么？
q_en: What does a Research Engineering interview usually focus on?
options: 只负责定义业务 KPI 指标，不涉及任何模型代码工作
只写 SQL 报表脚本，从不接触模型训练代码逻辑
实现和优化论文想法，做实验验证和 benchmark
只做人工标注团队的排期管理，不涉及实验和优化工作
options_en: Only defining business KPIs, with no model code work involved at all.
Only writing SQL report scripts, never touching model training code.
Implementing and optimizing research ideas, running experiments and benchmarks.
Only scheduling the manual labeling team, with no experiments or optimization.
why: 研究工程连接研究和软件工程，强调快速原型、性能优化和可复现的实验验证。
why_en: Research engineering sits between research and software engineering, emphasizing fast prototyping, performance optimization, and reproducible experiments.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用标准化任务和指标衡量系统性能的测试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A benchmark is a standardized test that measures a system's performance on a defined task and metric.

optionExplanations: 定 KPI 是产品/应用讨论的活，跟把论文想法跑通没有关系。
写报表是数据分析的工作，不涉及模型训练代码的实现和优化。
这正是研究工程的核心——把论文想法变成能跑、能验证的代码。
标注排期是数据团队的职责，研究工程要做的是实验和性能调优。
optionExplanations_en: Defining KPIs is product-discussion work and has nothing to do with getting a paper's idea running.
Writing reports is analytics work, not implementing or optimizing model training code.
This is the core of research engineering: turning a paper's idea into code you can run and verify.
Labeling schedules belong to the data team; research engineering is about running and tuning experiments.
scenario: 研究团队面你：要求两周内把一篇新论文复现出可对比的 benchmark 数字。
scenario_en: A research team is interviewing you: reproduce a new paper within two weeks and produce benchmark numbers you can compare against.

scenario: 你正在申请一个 mid-level ML 岗位，纠结要不要花时间准备 system design 环节。
scenario_en: You are applying for a mid-level ML role and deciding whether to spend time on system design prep.
q: 从职级规律看，你该怎么判断？
q_en: How should you judge this from the level pattern?
options: 只有拿到 offer 后才需要懂 system design
只有 research scientist 才会被考 system design
只有实习生会被考 system design
mid-level 起就该认真准备，senior 更是必考项
options_en: You only need this after you already have the offer.
Only research scientists get asked system design.
Only interns get asked system design.
Take it seriously from mid-level on; it is essentially mandatory at senior.
why: 入门 ML 岗位很少考 system design；到 mid-level 就常见，到 senior 基本是必考，所以越资深越不能跳过这块准备。
why_en: Entry-level ML roles rarely include system design, but it becomes common at mid-level and standard at senior, so this prep is not optional once you're past entry level.
optionExplanations: 面试就在拿 offer 之前进行，等拿到 offer 才准备已经来不及了。
应用型和 infra 岗位到中高级同样常被考 system design，不只是研究岗。
实习生通常不太会被考这块，中高级反而更常见。
职级越高，system design 权重越大，从 mid-level 起就不能跳过。
optionExplanations_en: The interview happens before you get the offer, so waiting for the offer to prep is already too late.
Applied and infra roles get tested on system design at mid-to-senior level too, not just research.
Interns are rarely tested on this; it's mid-to-senior candidates who see it more.
The more senior the role, the heavier this weighs, so it can't be skipped from mid-level on.

q: 面试官的 ML system design 打分表通常包含哪几个维度？（多选）
q_en: Which dimensions does an interviewer's ML system design scorecard usually contain? (Select all)
options: Problem Navigation
Input Data, Features, and Labels
Model Design
Integration and Evaluation
options_en: Problem Navigation, framing a vague goal as a measurable ML problem.
Input Data, Features, and Labels, finding and representing the right data.
Model Design, choosing and explaining model architecture and tradeoffs.
Integration and Evaluation, deploying, monitoring, and evaluating in production.
why: 这四个维度覆盖从模糊业务问题到生产闭环的核心能力，沟通是贯穿全程的隐性评估项。
why_en: These four dimensions cover the full path from a vague business problem to a production loop, while communication is assessed implicitly throughout.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Problem[Problem nav] --> Data[Data labels]
  Data --> Model[Model design]
  Model --> Eval[Integration eval]
  Eval --> Communicate[Communicate]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模糊业务目标转成可衡量 ML 问题的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Problem navigation is the ability to frame a vague business goal as a measurable ML problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 评估模型能否部署、监控、迭代并被正确衡量的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Integration and evaluation assesses whether a model can be deployed, monitored, iterated on, and measured correctly.

optionExplanations: Problem Navigation 考的是能不能把一个模糊目标拆成可衡量的 ML 问题。
Input Data, Features, and Labels 考的是找数据、设计标签和表示特征这条链路是否可信。
Model Design 考的是选架构时怎么权衡效果、成本和延迟。
Integration and Evaluation 考的是模型上线后怎么监控、迭代和衡量效果。
optionExplanations_en: Problem Navigation checks whether you can turn a vague goal into a measurable ML problem.
Input Data, Features, and Labels checks whether the data-to-label-to-feature chain is trustworthy.
Model Design checks how you trade off accuracy, cost, and latency when picking an architecture.
Integration and Evaluation checks how the model is monitored, iterated on, and measured after launch.
scenario: 你要给 60 分钟 ML system design 面试做自评表，按面试官打分的维度逐项检查自己的回答。
scenario_en: You are building a self-check sheet for a 60-minute ML system design interview, going through the dimensions an interviewer actually scores.

q: Problem Navigation 这个评估维度主要看什么？
q_en: What does the Problem Navigation dimension mainly test?
options: 能否在最短时间内背出最多的模型名称和论文引用清单
能否把模糊目标转成可衡量的 ML 问题并说明风险
能否写出响应速度最快的前端页面渲染代码
能否让面试官完全不追问任何一个细节问题
options_en: Reciting the longest list of model names and paper citations in the shortest time.
Framing a vague goal as a measurable ML problem and naming the risks.
Writing the fastest-rendering front-end page code.
Getting the interviewer to skip every single follow-up question.
why: 强候选人会明确 success metric、数据可得性，并讨论分类/排序/回归等不同 formulation 的取舍。
why_en: Problem navigation is about turning ambiguous goals into measurable ML problems while stating assumptions, risks, and formulation tradeoffs.
optionExplanations: 背模型名字和能不能把一个模糊问题拆清楚是两回事。
定指标、亮出假设、权衡不同 formulation，这才是这个维度真正在看的能力。
前端渲染速度不在系统设计面试的考察范围内。
回避追问在面试官眼里反而像是思路不清晰。
optionExplanations_en: Reciting model names is a different skill from breaking down an ambiguous problem.
Naming a metric, stating assumptions, and weighing formulations is what this dimension actually checks.
Frontend rendering speed is outside what a system design interview evaluates.
Dodging follow-ups reads as unclear thinking to the interviewer, not as strength.
scenario: 面试官只丢一句“提升 feed 参与度”，没给指标、没给数据，就让你开始设计。
scenario_en: The interviewer just says "improve feed engagement" — no metric, no data description — and asks you to start designing.

scenario: 业务方提出「提升用户体验」，但没有给出数据、可执行动作或成功标准。
scenario_en: The business asks to improve user experience, but gives no data, action, or success metric.
q: 强候选人应该先做什么？
q_en: What should a strong candidate do first?
options: 直接打开笔记本开始训练一个模型，完全不问业务目标
不问清楚业务需求，就默认套用一套推荐系统架构
先澄清可观测的成功指标，再判断 ML 是否适合
跳过目标讨论，只争论应该选用哪种神经网络架构
options_en: Open a notebook and start training a model immediately, without asking about the business goal.
Default to a recommendation-system architecture without confirming the actual business need.
First clarify a measurable success signal, then check whether ML fits.
Skip the goal discussion and only debate which neural network architecture to use.
why: 并非每个问题都该立即 ML 化；先定义可测目标、可用数据和可执行动作，才谈得上选 formulation。
why_en: Not every problem should jump straight to ML — first pin down a measurable goal, available data, and an actionable decision.
whenOtherWins: 如果问题已经有清晰标签和决策动作，可以更快跳到数据和模型选择。
tradeoff: 先澄清目标是否适合 ML vs 直接开始建模
optionExplanations: 没有成功标准就开始训练，很可能是在错的目标上花力气。
还没确认业务需求就套推荐架构，架构和真实需求可能对不上。
先把可衡量的成功指标定清楚，才谈得上判断这题该不该用 ML。
跳过目标直接争论网络结构，等于跳过了这题真正缺的那一步。
optionExplanations_en: Starting to train without a success criterion risks optimizing for the wrong target.
Defaulting to a recommender architecture before confirming the real need may not fit the actual problem.
Pinning down a measurable success signal first is what lets you judge whether ML even fits here.
Jumping straight to network architecture skips the step this scenario is actually missing.

q: Input Data, Features, and Labels 这个维度主要评估什么？
q_en: What does the Input Data, Features, and Labels dimension mainly assess?
options: 只看数据库表的大小和字段数量多少
只看模型有多少层、参数量有多大
只看候选人简历上写了多少年经验
招募有用数据、设计标签并表示好特征
options_en: Only the size of a database table and its column count.
Only how many layers the model has and its parameter count.
Only how many years of experience are on the resume.
Sourcing useful data, designing labels, and representing features.
why: 生产 ML 常败在数据而非模型：信号来源、标签质量、代理信号和特征表示都要说清楚。
why_en: Production ML often fails on data rather than modeling, so this dimension checks sourcing signal, label design, leakage, feedback loops, and feature representation.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Sources[Data sources] --> Labels[Labels proxies]
  Labels --> Features[Feature reps]
  Features --> Checks[Leakage checks]
  Checks --> Train[Training set]

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练数据中混入了预测时拿不到的未来信息，导致评估虚高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Data leakage means training data accidentally includes information unavailable at prediction time, inflating evaluation scores.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型的输出反过来影响后续收集到的数据，形成自我强化的偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feedback loop is when a model's own outputs influence the data collected later, creating self-reinforcing bias.

optionExplanations: 表有多大、字段有多少和数据本身的质量、标签设计没关系。
模型层数属于 Model Design 那个维度，不是这里在考的东西。
简历年限不是这个维度要评估的对象。
生产 ML 最常在数据这一环栽跟头，这一项正好对上这个风险。
optionExplanations_en: Table size and column count have nothing to do with data quality or label design.
Layer count belongs to the Model Design dimension, not what's being tested here.
Years on a resume aren't what this dimension is checking.
Production ML most often fails on the data side, and this option covers exactly that risk.
scenario: 同一道 feed 排序题，面试官追问训练样本从哪来、正负标签怎么定、有没有泄漏。
scenario_en: On that same feed ranking question, the interviewer drills into where training samples come from, how labels are defined, and whether anything leaks.

scenario: 视频推荐没有用户显式评分，但有观看时长、跳出和分享行为数据。
scenario_en: A video recommender has no explicit ratings, but it has watch time, bounce, and share behavior.
q: 这些行为数据在建模中扮演什么角色？
q_en: What role do these behavior signals play in modeling?
options: 这些行为数据完全无用，必须直接丢弃
可作为代理标签/隐式反馈来监督模型
应该直接当作模型的超参数来调
只能用来监控服务器和基础设施的运行指标
options_en: These behavior signals are completely useless and should be discarded outright.
Usable as proxy labels or implicit feedback for supervision.
Should be treated directly as hyperparameters to tune the model.
Only useful for monitoring server and infrastructure health metrics.
why: 隐式反馈能监督推荐模型，但带偏差和噪声，面试要说明如何利用和校正。
why_en: Implicit signals like watch time and shares can serve as proxy labels for supervision, though they carry bias and noise that need correction.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务要求判定内容是否违规，代理标签不能替代高质量人工标注。
tradeoff: 低成本的隐式行为信号 vs 高置信度的人工标签

termDefinitions.meaning: 用容易获得的间接信号代替真正想预测的目标当作标签。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A proxy label is an easy-to-collect indirect signal used as a stand-in for the true target you want to predict.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户行为中隐含的偏好信号，例如观看、点击、跳出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Implicit feedback is a preference signal inferred from user behavior, such as watches, clicks, or bounces.

optionExplanations: 丢掉这些信号，就丢掉了在没有显式评分时唯一能用的监督来源。
观看时长、跳出、分享这类行为可以当代理标签，训练排序模型时能派上用场。
行为数据是拿来监督模型的信号，不是用来调参的超参数。
这类数据的价值主要在训练模型上，不只是拿来看基础设施健不健康。
optionExplanations_en: Discarding these signals throws away the only supervision source you have without explicit ratings.
Watch time, bounces, and shares can serve as proxy labels for training a ranking model.
Behavior data is a supervision signal for the model, not a knob you tune.
This data's main value is training the model, not just checking infra health.

q: Model Design 这个维度的核心是什么？
q_en: What is the core of the Model Design dimension?
options: 综合成本、延迟和可解释性选架构并解释取舍
永远选择参数量最大的那一个模型
只写训练脚本，完全不讨论架构选择问题
只关心模型发布时的版本号数字
options_en: Weigh cost, latency, and interpretability, and explain the tradeoffs.
Always pick whichever model has the most parameters.
Only write training scripts, never discuss architecture choices.
Only care about the model's release version number.
why: 模型设计要兼顾效果、成本、延迟和可解释性，复杂不等于更好，多组件系统还要讲清楚怎么配合。
why_en: Model design weighs accuracy against cost, latency, and interpretability, and complexity is not automatically better.
optionExplanations: 这正是模型设计要展示的能力——多个约束一起权衡，还要讲清各组件怎么配合。
参数量越大不代表效果越好，生产环境的延迟和成本经常撑不住。
只写脚本不谈架构，等于跳过了面试真正想看的判断力。
版本号是发布管理的事实题，和架构判断没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly what model design tests — weighing several constraints together and explaining how components fit.
More parameters doesn't mean better; production latency and cost budgets often can't absorb it.
Writing only scripts without discussing architecture skips the judgment the interview wants to see.
A version number is a release-management fact, unrelated to architecture judgment.
scenario: feed 排序要在 100ms 内返回，运营还要能解释为什么推这条，预算不允许最大模型。
scenario_en: Feed ranking must return within 100ms, ops needs to explain why an item was shown, and the budget rules out the largest model.

scenario: 你只做过推荐系统，现在被问到一个 fraud detection 的题目。
scenario_en: You have only worked on recommendation systems, and now the interviewer asks about fraud detection.
q: 为什么不应该用「我只做过推荐」自我设限？
q_en: Why should you not limit yourself by saying you only worked on recommendations?
options: 因为推荐经验在新领域完全不重要
因为面试官不会追问任何细节
因为面试看重能否把通用原则迁移到新场景
因为所有 ML 问题的解法其实都一样
options_en: Recommendation experience is completely irrelevant in a new domain.
Interviewers will not probe for any details.
Interviewers value whether you can transfer general principles to a new scenario.
Every ML problem actually has the same solution.
why: 强候选人会把数据、特征、评估、反馈循环等通用原则迁移到 fraud、moderation 等新场景，而不是止步于熟悉领域。
why_en: Strong candidates transfer general principles — data, features, evaluation, feedback loops — to unfamiliar domains instead of stopping at what they know.
optionExplanations: 把经验说得完全不重要，反而丢掉了本来可以迁移的那部分能力。
面试官通常会顺着细节继续追问，借此判断你理解的深度。
这正是面试真正想看的——能不能把数据、特征这类原则套到新场景上。
不同 ML 问题在数据和风险上差别很大，不是同一套解法能通吃的。
optionExplanations_en: Calling the experience entirely irrelevant throws away the part that actually transfers.
Interviewers usually keep probing on details to gauge how deep your understanding goes.
This is exactly what's being tested — whether data and feature principles carry over to a new domain.
Different ML problems differ a lot in data and risk, so one solution doesn't fit every case.

scenario: 你做过分类系统，但题目换成了推荐系统设计。
scenario_en: You have built classification systems, but the prompt is now a recommendation-system design.
q: 更好的开场表达是？
q_en: What is a better opening response?
options: 说明自己对细节不熟悉，但用已知原则继续推理
说自己完全不会，然后停止作答
把推荐问题强行当二分类处理，不解释理由
只反复讲过去做过的分类项目
options_en: State that you're unfamiliar with the details, then keep reasoning from transferable principles.
Say you don't know it at all and stop answering.
Force the recommendation problem into a binary classifier without explaining why.
Keep repeating the classification project you've already done.
why: 诚实说明边界、再用可迁移原则推理，能给面试官清楚的信号；不要让陌生领域打断结构化思考。
why_en: State your boundary honestly, then reason forward with transferable principles like supervision signals and serving constraints, instead of stalling.
whenOtherWins: 如果岗位明确要求推荐系统专家，还是要补齐排序、召回这类核心 recsys 概念。
tradeoff: 承认边界+通用原则推理 vs 假装熟悉却讲不出细节

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量排序结果质量的指标，例如 NDCG、precision@k。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ranking metric measures the quality of an ordered list, such as NDCG or precision at k.

optionExplanations: 先说清楚边界，再用监督信号、服务约束这类通用原则往下推，既诚实又展示了思路。
说完全不会就停下来，面试官就拿不到任何可以评估的推理过程了。
推荐和分类的目标不一样，硬套二分类框架会漏掉召回、排序这些关键约束。
只讲旧项目而不接招新题目，等于没有回答面试官真正问的推荐设计。
optionExplanations_en: Naming the boundary, then reasoning forward with transferable principles like supervision signals, is honest and still shows structure.
Saying you can't do it and stopping gives the interviewer no reasoning process to evaluate.
Recommendation and classification have different goals, so forcing a binary frame misses ranking and recall constraints.
Repeating an old project without engaging the new prompt never actually answers the recommender question.

q: Integration and Evaluation 这个维度评估什么？
q_en: What does the Integration and Evaluation dimension assess?
options: 只看离线 notebook 里的评估分数
模型如何部署、监控、迭代，并设计合适评估
只看训练集上的准确率数字
只看数据表的数量和字段
options_en: Only the score shown in an offline notebook run.
How the model is deployed, monitored, iterated on, with a fitting evaluation design.
Only the accuracy number on the training set.
Only the number of columns in a data table.
why: 生产和 notebook 之间有很大差距：延迟、成本、漂移、实验设计、监控和回滚都要考虑。
why_en: There is a real gap between a notebook result and production, so this dimension covers deployment, monitoring, iteration, and evaluation design.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Train[Train] --> Deploy[Deploy]
  Deploy --> Monitor[Monitor]
  Monitor --> Evaluate[Evaluate]
  Evaluate --> Retrain[Retrain]

termDefinitions.meaning: 线上数据分布随时间偏离训练时的分布，导致模型效果下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Drift is when live data distribution shifts away from training data over time, degrading model performance.

optionExplanations: notebook 里的分数证明不了模型上线后真的有业务价值。
这正是这个维度要考的——从上线到监控、迭代的完整闭环。
训练集准确率容易过拟合，不能代表线上的真实表现。
表的数量跟模型能不能部署、监控没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: A notebook score can't prove the model creates real value once it's live.
This is exactly what the dimension tests — the full loop from launch through monitoring and iteration.
Training-set accuracy is prone to overfitting and doesn't reflect live performance.
Table count has nothing to do with whether a model can be deployed or monitored.
scenario: 你的排序模型离线 AUC 涨了 3 个点，面试官问上线后怎么证明业务指标真的涨了。
scenario_en: Your ranking model gains three points of offline AUC, and the interviewer asks how you would prove the business metric actually moved after launch.

scenario: 模型在 notebook 里的指标很好，但还没有上线、监控和 A/B 实验设计。
scenario_en: The model has strong notebook metrics, but there is no launch plan, monitoring, or A/B test design yet.
q: 面试官会认为这暴露了什么风险？
q_en: What risk would the interviewer see here?
options: 这些离线指标一定比上线后的真实数据更可信
这个模型的开发工作已经算完成了
接下来完全不需要再做任何评估
无法证明它能在生产中真正产生业务价值
options_en: These offline metrics are more trustworthy than real production data would be.
The model's development work is already considered done.
No further evaluation is needed from here on.
It cannot prove the model will create real business value in production.
why: 应用型 ML 不是实验结束就算成功，还要服务、度量和迭代；缺这些会让方案停在 notebook 阶段。
why_en: Applied ML is not done when the experiment ends — without serving, monitoring, and evaluation design, you cannot prove production business value.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目明确只考研究验证，生产闭环这块的权重会降低。
tradeoff: notebook 里的离线指标 vs 生产环境的真实业务价值
optionExplanations: 线下指标常常测不出真实分布和延迟，不会比上线后的数字更可信。
实验做完不等于模型完成，离真正服务用户还差一大截。
跳过评估设计，业务方就没法判断这东西到底该不该上线。
少了服务、监控和实验这几步，这个方案的业务价值就还没法验证。
optionExplanations_en: Offline metrics often miss real distribution shifts and latency, so they're not more trustworthy than live numbers.
Finishing the experiment isn't the same as finishing the model; there's still a gap before it serves real users.
Skipping evaluation design leaves the business with no way to judge whether it's ready to launch.
Without serving, monitoring, and experiments, this solution's business value stays unproven.

q: 沟通能力为什么是所有 ML 面试的隐含评估项？
q_en: Why is communication an implicit evaluation in every ML interview?
options: 因为沟通只影响回答时的语速快慢
因为答案本身是固定的，不需要交流对齐
因为系统设计要协作解决模糊问题、对齐取舍
因为完全不需要听面试官提出的追问
options_en: Communication only affects how fast you talk.
The answer itself is fixed, so no real exchange is needed.
Design is collaborative work on ambiguity that needs aligning tradeoffs.
You don't need to listen to the interviewer's follow-ups at all.
why: 面试官会观察你如何回应 probe、调整方向、承认假设和解释 tradeoff，这些都是沟通信号。
why_en: Interviewers implicitly watch how you respond to probes, adjust direction, and explain tradeoffs, all of which are communication signals.
optionExplanations: 语速快慢和你能不能讲清假设、取舍其实没什么关系。
系统设计本来就没有唯一固定答案，全程都要靠交流对齐。
系统设计是协作解决模糊问题的过程，全程都要不断校准假设和取舍。
忽略追问会让你的方向偏离面试官真正关心的地方。
optionExplanations_en: Talking speed has little to do with whether you can explain your assumptions and tradeoffs clearly.
System design has no single fixed answer to begin with, so alignment happens through conversation.
System design is a collaborative process on ambiguous problems, so you're continuously calibrating assumptions and tradeoffs.
Ignoring follow-ups drifts your answer away from what the interviewer actually cares about.
scenario: 面试进行到一半，面试官突然把范围从全球用户改成只做一个国家，还追问你的假设。
scenario_en: Halfway through, the interviewer shrinks scope from global users to a single country and starts probing your assumptions.

q: 按文章建议的准备路径排序。
q_en: Order the prep path recommended by the article.
why: 先确认考什么，再用框架组织表达，补核心知识，最后通过互动练习应对 probe。
why_en: Preparation should start with the interview type, then the framework, core concepts, and interactive practice.
tradeoff: 先诊断面试类型 vs 直接套用统一模板
steps: 阅读核心概念和常见模式
练习 problem breakdown 并与朋友/mentor 互动
根据岗位确认面试类型

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试作答时用来组织表达顺序的结构化框架。

q: 按一次应用型 ML 方案的自然评估链排序。
q_en: Order the natural evaluation chain for an applied ML solution.
why: 这对应从模糊问题到生产系统的完整路径。每一步都影响下一步质量。
why_en: An applied ML solution flows from problem framing to data, model design, and production evaluation.
tradeoff: 先定义目标 vs 先选模型架构

scenario: 你想在面试里表达「先判断任务类型，再选模型」这个思路。
scenario_en: You want to show the interviewer that you choose the ML task type before choosing a model.
q: 这段伪代码体现什么面试思路？
q_en: What interview habit does this pseudocode show?
options: 从模型名字反推出业务目标
随机选择一个任务类型
从产品动作推导 ML 任务类型
只优化参数量而不管任务类型
options_en: Infer the business goal backward from the model's name.
Pick a task type at random.
Derive the ML task type from the product action.
Only optimize parameter count, ignoring task type.
why: ML 任务类型应由产品动作和目标决定：排序列表、二元动作、数值预测分别对应 ranking、classification、regression。
why_en: The ML task type should be derived from the product action — ranking a list, a binary decision, or predicting a number map to ranking, classification, or regression.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统有多阶段组件，可能同时包含分类、召回、排序和回归。
tradeoff: 从产品动作反推 formulation vs 从模型名字或参数量反推目标

termDefinitions.meaning: 把业务问题表述成具体的 ML 任务类型，例如分类、排序或回归。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Formulation is expressing a business problem as a concrete ML task type, such as classification, ranking, or regression.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测一个连续数值的建模任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Regression is a modeling task that predicts a continuous numeric value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把输入判给一个或多个离散类别的建模任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Classification is a modeling task that assigns input to one or more discrete categories.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一组候选按相关性或质量排序的建模任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ranking is a modeling task that orders a set of candidates by relevance or quality.

optionExplanations: 模型名字是推导出来的结果，拿它反推业务目标，顺序整个反了。
随便选一个任务类型，formulation 就跟产品真正要做的事脱节了。
代码正是照这个顺序走的：先看产品动作是排序、拦截还是预测数值，再选对应的任务类型。
参数量大小和该选哪种任务类型，是两件不搭边的事。
optionExplanations_en: The model name is a downstream result, so working backward from it reverses the actual reasoning order.
Picking a task type at random disconnects the formulation from what the product is actually trying to do.
This mirrors the code's order: look at whether the product action ranks, blocks, or predicts a value, then pick the matching task type.
Parameter count and which task type to pick are two unrelated decisions.

q: Applied ML 面试通常会考哪些能力？（多选）
q_en: Which skills are usually tested in an Applied ML interview? (Select all)
options: 业务问题到 ML 方案
数据、预处理和特征
模型选择、训练和评估
部署和监控
options_en: Translating a business problem into an ML solution.
Data, preprocessing, and feature engineering.
Model selection, training, and evaluation.
Deployment and monitoring.
why: 这四项能力构成生产 ML 闭环，只擅长其中一块通常撑不起完整的系统设计面试。
why_en: These four skills form the full production ML loop, and being strong in only one rarely carries a system design interview.
optionExplanations: 把业务问题转成 ML 方案是应用型面试的起点，没有这步后面都白搭。
数据、预处理和特征工程决定了模型能不能学到真正有用的信号。
模型选择、训练和评估要在效果、成本、延迟之间做取舍。
部署和监控决定了模型上线后能不能持续可靠地跑下去。
optionExplanations_en: Turning a business problem into an ML solution is the starting point; skip it and everything after is off-target.
Data, preprocessing, and feature engineering decide whether the model can learn a genuinely useful signal.
Model selection, training, and evaluation require trading off accuracy against cost and latency.
Deployment and monitoring decide whether the model keeps running reliably once it's live.
scenario: 你只剩两周准备一场 Applied ML 面试，要决定复习清单覆盖哪几块能力。
scenario_en: You have two weeks left before an applied ML interview and must decide which areas your study list should cover.

scenario: 你在用一份专注生产落地技能、不讲理论证明的 ML 面试指南备考。
scenario_en: You are using an ML interview guide focused on production skills, not theory proofs.
q: 这类指南通常不适合作为哪类面试组合的主要准备材料？
q_en: For which interview mix is this guide usually not enough as the main prep material?
options: Applied ML System Design
AI/ML Research 和 Research Engineering
ML Infra Design
Applied ML System Design 和 ML Infra Design
options_en: Applied ML System Design.
AI/ML Research and Research Engineering.
ML Infra Design.
Applied ML System Design and ML Infra Design.
why: 指南对研究和研究工程不是主线，因为它不深入理论创新、论文实现或性能优化。
why_en: The guide is not the main prep path for AI/ML research or research engineering because it does not go deep on theory, papers, or performance optimization.
tradeoff: 应用型生产设计深度 vs 理论研究/论文实现深度
optionExplanations: 这正是指南的主线，不是它覆盖不到的类型。
这两类更看重原创理论、论文复现和极致性能调优，指南在这块讲得比较浅。
指南对 infra 面试仍然部分适用，不是完全覆盖不到。
这两类反而是指南覆盖最多、最核心的部分。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly the guide's main track, not the type it fails to cover.
These two tracks lean on original theory, reproducing papers, and heavy performance tuning, areas this guide only skims.
The guide is still partly useful for infra interviews, not fully unhelpful.
These two are actually the guide's strongest and most central coverage.

scenario: 你一进面试就说「我只做过实现，可能不适合这个系统设计」。
scenario_en: At the start of the interview, you say, "I only implemented systems, so I may not be a fit for this design round."
q: 这样开场有什么问题？
q_en: What is wrong with opening this way?
options: 会自动帮你加分
能替代和面试官澄清题目范围
会在面试官评估你之前，先削弱自己的信号
能减少后续所有 follow-up 问题
options_en: It automatically earns bonus points.
It can replace clarifying scope with the recruiter beforehand.
It weakens your signal before the interviewer can even assess you.
It reduces every follow-up question afterward.
why: 公司邀请你面试就说明他们认为你有机会合适；面试中途自我贬低只会在评估前先扣分。
why_en: Being invited to interview already signals the company thinks you might be a fit, so pre-qualifying yourself negatively only weakens your signal before they can assess you.
whenOtherWins: 如果某个具体知识点确实不熟，可以就那一点坦诚说明，再继续推理，而不是整体自我否定。
tradeoff: 面试前和 recruiter 澄清范围 vs 面试中用不确定性自我设限
optionExplanations: 自我贬低不会加分，面试官通常会照实评估你接下来的表现。
澄清范围应该提前找 recruiter 谈，不是靠面试中说一句不确定带过。
公司愿意面试你，已经说明他们觉得你有机会合适，开场自贬等于提前给自己扣分。
追问的多少取决于题目本身的深度，不会因为一句自我贬低就减少。
optionExplanations_en: Self-deprecation doesn't earn bonus points; interviewers still grade what you do next on its own merits.
Scope should be clarified with the recruiter ahead of time, not waved off with a line of self-doubt mid-interview.
Getting the invite already means they think you could be a fit; opening with doubt just costs you points early.
Follow-up depth tracks the problem itself, not how the opening line sounded.

q: 为什么练习时要找朋友或 mentor 一起做，而不是自己对着题目默写？
q_en: Why practice with a friend or mentor instead of silently writing answers alone?
options: 面试高度互动，回应追问和协作同样重要
熟悉的朋友或 mentor 可以代替你去参加真正的面试
只要多陪练几次，就可以不用再自己学习基础知识
找人陪练主要是为了方便掐时间
options_en: The interview is highly interactive, so responding to follow-ups and collaborating matter just as much.
A friend or mentor you trust can attend the real interview in your place.
Enough practice sessions with a partner remove the need to ever learn fundamentals yourself.
The main point of a practice partner is just to keep time conveniently.
why: 真实面试不是独白，面试官会不断改变范围或追问；练习互动能训练临场表达和调整能力。
why_en: A real interview is not a monologue — interviewers keep probing and shifting scope, so practicing interactively trains you to respond and adjust.
optionExplanations: 这正是陪练要练的东西——怎么回应追问、怎么跟人协作调整方向。
真正上场终究要你自己应对，朋友没法替你面试。
陪练能练表达，但基础概念还是得自己先学扎实。
掐时间只是陪练顺带的好处，不是找人一起练的主要原因。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly what practicing with a partner trains: responding to probes and adjusting direction together.
The real interview still has to be you in the room; a friend can't sit in for you.
Practicing with someone sharpens delivery, but fundamentals still need to be learned solo first.
Timing is a nice side effect, not the actual reason to practice with a partner.
scenario: 你还剩一周备考，每天只有一小时练习，要在默写答案和找人陪练之间选一种方式。
scenario_en: With one week left and only an hour a day to practice, you must choose between writing answers alone and drilling with a partner.

scenario: 同一道模糊的业务问题分别抛给 mid-level 和 senior 候选人。
scenario_en: The same vague business problem is given to a mid-level candidate and a senior candidate.
q: 两者被期待的表现有什么不同？
q_en: How are the expected performances different?
options: 两者被期待的表现完全一样，职级不影响评分标准
senior 需要更独立地导航模糊性并提出假设
mid-level 面试反而要承担比 senior 更多的模糊性
两者都可以完全依赖面试官主动喂细节
options_en: Both levels are expected to perform identically, with level not affecting the rubric.
Senior candidates must navigate ambiguity more independently and propose their own assumptions.
Mid-level interviews actually carry more ambiguity than senior ones do.
Both levels can fully rely on the interviewer volunteering the details.
why: 越资深，越要能在不完整信息下自己定目标、约束和风险；模板只是支架，不是终点。
why_en: The more senior you are, the more you're expected to navigate ambiguity yourself and land on a high-leverage formulation.
tradeoff: senior 自主导航模糊性 vs mid-level 依赖更清晰的问题设定
optionExplanations: 如果表现期待真的一样，同一道题对 senior 就不该有更高要求，但实际不是这样。
职级越高，越要能在信息不全的情况下自己定目标、提假设、扛风险。
通常是 senior 面对的问题更模糊，而不是反过来。
越资深越要主动定义问题，不能一直等面试官喂细节。
optionExplanations_en: If expectations were truly identical, the same problem wouldn't demand more from senior candidates, but it clearly does.
The more senior the role, the more you're expected to set goals, assumptions, and risks yourself under incomplete information.
Usually it's the senior candidate who faces more ambiguity, not the other way around.
The more senior you are, the more you're expected to define the problem yourself, not wait for details.

scenario: 你备考时间有限，只能强化最能提升 ML system design 表现的基础。
scenario_en: Your prep time is limited, so you can only strengthen the foundations that most improve ML system design performance.
q: 根据文章建议，你应该优先打磨什么组合？
q_en: Based on the article, which combination should you prioritize?
options: 只背诵经典论文里的引用清单
只反复刷力扣风格的算法与数据结构题目
只学习网页界面设计的排版规范
框架 + 核心概念 + 实战演练
options_en: Only memorize the citation list from classic papers.
Only grind LeetCode-style algorithm and data-structure problems.
Only study web page layout and UI design guidelines.
A delivery framework, core concepts, and hands-on rehearsal.
why: 面试需要结构、知识和表达练习共同作用：框架给流程，概念给取舍词汇，walkthrough 给迁移能力。
why_en: Interview performance needs structure, vocabulary, and rehearsed practice together — a delivery framework, core concepts, and problem walkthroughs.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标公司明确侧重研究论文，理论和论文阅读的权重要相应提高。
tradeoff: 结构化框架+核心概念+实战演练 vs 单点技能（论文/算法题/UI规范）
optionExplanations: 论文引用和系统设计面试要展示的表达能力关联很弱。
算法题考的是另一种能力，系统设计还要结构和取舍语言。
界面设计规范根本不在 ML system design 的考察范围里。
三者一起补，才凑得齐面试真正要看的流程、词汇和临场迁移能力。
optionExplanations_en: Paper citations correlate weakly with the delivery skill a system design interview actually tests.
Algorithm drills build a different skill; system design also needs structure and tradeoff vocabulary.
UI design guidelines aren't part of what ML system design assesses at all.
Covering all three together is what supplies the flow, vocabulary, and on-the-fly transfer the interview wants.

scenario: 为支付平台做欺诈检测，标签是「30 天内被判定为欺诈」。有人把「账号已被风控团队冻结」这一字段当作特征，而冻结动作发生在欺诈被判定之后。
scenario_en: For payment fraud detection, the label is "ruled fraudulent within 30 days". Someone adds "account frozen by the risk team" as a feature — but freezing only happens after fraud is confirmed.
q: 这个特征进入训练集后，模型会以什么方式坏掉？
q_en: How exactly does the model break once this feature enters the training set?
options: 离线指标虚高，线上打分时该字段还是空的，拦截率掉回基线
训练阶段会直接抛类型错误，特征列和标签列对不上，管线跑不完就中断
只会带来轻微过拟合，把正则化系数调大一点，线上表现就能恢复
推理延迟明显升高，因为每次打分都要多查一次风控系统的冻结状态表
options_en: Offline metrics look inflated, but the field is still empty at scoring time, so catch rate falls back to baseline.
Training throws a type error because the feature column and the label column do not line up, and the pipeline aborts.
It only causes mild overfitting; raising the regularization strength restores production performance.
Inference latency climbs because every scoring call has to make an extra lookup against the risk system freeze table.
why: 冻结发生在判定之后，把它当特征等于把标签的未来信息灌进训练集；代价是离线 AUC 好看，线上这个字段还没被填上，模型退化成基线。
why_en: The freeze happens after the label is decided, so using it as a feature leaks the label's future into training; offline AUC looks great while production scoring sees an empty field.

termDefinitions.meaning: 特征里混入了只有在标签确定之后才存在的信息，训练时可见、预测时不可得。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Label leakage is when a feature carries information that only exists after the label is known, so it is available in training but not at prediction time.

termDefinitions.meaning: Area Under the ROC Curve（ROC 曲线下面积）：衡量模型区分正负样本能力的离线指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC stands for Area Under the ROC Curve, an offline metric for how well a model separates positive from negative examples.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在损失函数里加惩罚项，限制模型复杂度以抑制过拟合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Regularization adds a penalty term to the loss so the model stays simpler and overfits less.

optionExplanations: 训练时字段已填、预测时字段还没产生，这条时间差就是离线线上落差的来源。
泄漏是语义问题不是类型问题，列的 dtype 完全合法，管线不会报任何错。
正则化管的是模型太复杂，管不了输入本身就带着答案，调参再多也没用。
多查一张表只是工程开销；就算查得飞快，这个特征在打分时刻依然是空的。
optionExplanations_en: The field is populated in training but not yet created at prediction time — that time gap is exactly the offline-online gap.
Leakage is a semantic problem, not a typing one; the column dtype is perfectly valid and nothing errors out.
Regularization fights model complexity, not an input that already contains the answer; no amount of tuning fixes it.
An extra table lookup is just engineering overhead; even a fast lookup returns nothing at scoring time.

scenario: 电商推荐每晚用当天的曝光点击日志重训模型，而当天的曝光完全由前一版模型决定。几周后候选商品的种类越来越窄。
scenario_en: An e-commerce recommender retrains nightly on that day's impression-click logs, but those impressions are chosen entirely by the previous model. After a few weeks the candidate set keeps narrowing.
q: 这个收窄过程在数据层面是怎么一步步发生的？
q_en: Step by step, how does that narrowing happen at the data level?
options: 没被推荐过的商品拿不到曝光，日志里永远没有它们的正样本，模型不断自我确认
训练集每天变大直到超出单机内存，采样比例被迫下调，模型因为样本变少而欠拟合
用户口味本身在几周内收敛了，模型只是忠实地反映了这个真实的需求变化
夜间重训的时间窗太短，梯度还没收敛就被迫停止，参数每天都停在不同的位置
options_en: Items never recommended get no impressions, so the logs never contain positives for them and the model keeps confirming itself.
The training set grows past single-machine memory each day, forcing a lower sampling rate, and the model underfits on fewer examples.
User taste genuinely converged over those weeks, and the model is only faithfully reflecting that real shift in demand.
The nightly retraining window is too short, so gradients stop before convergence and parameters land somewhere different each day.
why: 训练数据由模型自己的输出筛选出来，形成反馈回路：未曝光商品既无点击也无展示，下一轮更不会被选中。代价是必须留出一小部分随机曝光流量去采集反事实样本。
why_en: The training data is filtered by the model's own output, so unexposed items never earn clicks and get picked even less next round; breaking it costs a slice of random exposure traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型的输出决定了下一轮训练数据的采集范围，偏差被逐轮放大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feedback loop is when a model's own output decides what training data gets collected next, amplifying its bias each round.

termDefinitions.meaning: 商品被真实展示给用户的一次机会，只有曝光过的商品才可能产生点击标签。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An impression is one real chance for an item to be shown to a user; only impressed items can ever produce a click label.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型容量或数据不足，连训练集上的规律都没学到。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Underfitting means the model fails to capture patterns even on the training set, usually from too little capacity or data.

optionExplanations: 缺的是「没被展示过会不会被点」的反事实数据，样本再多也补不上这一块。
内存瓶颈会让指标整体变差，但不会专门让候选品类单向收窄。
如果真是需求变化，随机曝光流量上的点击率也会同步下降，实际不会。
训练不充分表现为指标抖动，不会稳定朝着「越来越窄」一个方向走。
optionExplanations_en: What is missing is counterfactual data — would an unshown item have been clicked — and more samples cannot supply it.
A memory bottleneck degrades metrics across the board; it would not narrow the category mix in one direction.
If demand had truly shifted, click rate on the random-exposure slice would drop too, and it does not.
Undertrained models show noisy metrics, not a steady one-way drift toward a narrower catalog.

scenario: 推荐模型要把 500 万个商品 ID 喂进神经网络，且新商品每天上架，需要靠共现行为学到商品之间的相似性。
scenario_en: A recommender must feed 5 million product IDs into a neural network, new items launch daily, and item-to-item similarity has to be learned from co-occurrence behaviour.
q: 这个高基数 ID 特征该用什么表示方式？
q_en: How should this high-cardinality ID feature be represented?
options: 学习一个低维 embedding 表，让相似商品在向量空间里靠近
直接用 one-hot 编码，为每个商品 ID 开一列二值特征输入模型
把商品 ID 当成整数直接输入，让模型自己从数值大小里学出关系
按上架时间给商品 ID 排序编号，用排名的百分位数当作单个连续特征
options_en: Learn a low-dimensional embedding table so similar products sit close together in vector space.
Use one-hot encoding directly, giving every product ID its own binary column into the model.
Feed the product ID in as a plain integer and let the model learn relationships from its magnitude.
Rank product IDs by launch date and feed the percentile of that rank as a single continuous feature.
why: 基数 500 万且要表达相似性，embedding 用几十维稠密向量承载共现结构；代价是要额外维护 embedding 表、处理新商品的冷启动初始化。
why_en: With five million values and a need to express similarity, an embedding packs co-occurrence structure into a few dozen dense dimensions, at the cost of maintaining the table and cold-starting new items.
tradeoff: embedding 的稠密低维表示与相似性泛化 vs one-hot 的稀疏正交表示与零训练成本
whenOtherWins: 如果这个类别特征只有十几个取值（例如设备类型），one-hot 更省事，不用训练也不会有冷启动问题。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把离散取值映射成一个可训练的低维稠密向量，语义相近的取值向量也相近。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding maps a discrete value to a trainable low-dimensional dense vector, so semantically similar values end up close together.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个取值开一列，命中的那列置 1、其余为 0，任意两个取值都彼此正交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: One-hot encoding gives each value its own column set to 1 while the rest are 0, leaving any two values mutually orthogonal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个类别特征可能取值的总个数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality is the total number of distinct values a categorical feature can take.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新出现的实体还没有行为数据，向量或统计特征都没法直接算出来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cold start is when a newly created entity has no behavioural history yet, so its vector or statistics cannot be computed directly.

optionExplanations: 几十维就装下 500 万个 ID，且相似商品共享方向，共现信息才有地方落。
取值少时它最省事，但这里会撑出 500 万列稀疏输入，且任意两商品距离恒等。
整数大小在这里没有真实含义，模型会误学出「ID 越大越相关」的假顺序。
上架时间的排名和商品相似性无关，压成一维等于把区分信息全丢掉。
optionExplanations_en: A few dozen dimensions hold all five million IDs, and similar items share directions so co-occurrence has somewhere to live.
It is simplest for small vocabularies, but here it blows up to five million sparse columns with equal distance between any two items.
Integer magnitude carries no real meaning here, so the model learns a fake ordering where bigger IDs look more related.
Launch-date rank has nothing to do with item similarity, and squashing to one dimension discards the distinguishing signal.

scenario: 面试题是欺诈检测，正样本占比不到 1%。候选人直接搬出上一题内容推荐用的评估方案：看整体 accuracy，再跑一次 A/B 测试。
scenario_en: The interview problem is fraud detection where positives are under 1% of traffic. The candidate reuses the evaluation plan from a content-recommendation question: overall accuracy plus an A/B test.
q: 面试官会先质疑这套评估方案的哪一点？
q_en: Which part of that evaluation plan will the interviewer question first?
options: accuracy 在这个正负比例下不区分模型，全判负也有 99% 以上
A/B 测试的样本量算法在欺诈场景里和推荐场景里用的是完全不同的统计公式
评估必须先离线跑完全部历史数据才可以上线，否则任何指标都不可信
每个 ML 问题都应该固定用一套通用评估模板，候选人这里选错了模板的版本
options_en: Accuracy separates nothing at this class ratio — predicting all-negative already scores above 99%.
The sample-size formula for an A/B test in fraud uses completely different statistics than in recommendation.
Evaluation must replay the entire history offline before any launch, otherwise no metric can be trusted at all.
Every ML problem should use one fixed universal evaluation template, and the candidate simply picked the wrong version of it.
why: 每个问题的评估策略都要按它的类别分布和业务代价重新设计，欺诈场景应该看 precision/recall 或召回在固定误报率下的表现；代价是要和业务确定一个可接受的误报预算。
why_en: Each problem needs an evaluation strategy built from its own class balance and business costs; fraud needs precision and recall at a fixed false-positive budget, which the business has to agree on.
tradeoff: 按问题定制的指标（分类不平衡下的 precision/recall）vs 跨题复用的通用指标（accuracy）
whenOtherWins: 如果正负样本大致平衡且两类错误代价相当（例如图片二分类质检），accuracy 就是最容易沟通的单一指标。

termDefinitions.meaning: 准确率：预测正确的样本占全部样本的比例，在类别极不平衡时会被多数类主导。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Accuracy is the share of all predictions that are correct, and it gets dominated by the majority class when data is heavily imbalanced.

termDefinitions.meaning: 精确率：被判为正的样本里真正为正的比例，对应误报代价。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision is the fraction of predicted positives that are truly positive, and it tracks the cost of false alarms.

termDefinitions.meaning: 召回率：全部真正样本里被模型抓到的比例，对应漏放代价。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall is the fraction of all true positives the model actually catches, tracking the cost of misses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把流量随机分成对照组和实验组，比较线上业务指标的差异。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An A/B test randomly splits traffic into control and treatment groups and compares live business metrics.

optionExplanations: 多数类占 99% 时，一个什么都不做的模型也能刷到高分，指标失去判别力。
A/B 的统计方法两边其实同源，真正变的是要看哪个指标，不是公式。
离线全量回放成本高又不必要，采样评估加上线上灰度就够支撑决策。
文章明确说每个问题都需要不同的评估策略，通用模板这个前提本身就不成立。
optionExplanations_en: When the majority class is 99%, a do-nothing model still scores high, so the metric loses all discriminating power.
The A/B statistics are the same on both sides; what actually changes is which metric you read, not the formula.
Replaying the whole history offline is expensive and unnecessary — sampled evaluation plus a staged rollout supports the decision.
The article says each problem needs its own evaluation strategy, so the universal-template premise is wrong to begin with.

scenario: 内容审核系统由三段串联：先用规则和轻模型召回可疑内容，再用分类模型打分，最后把高分内容送人审队列。团队把分类模型单独调到了历史最好水平，端到端漏放率却几乎没降。
scenario_en: A content moderation system chains three stages: cheap retrieval of suspicious content, a classifier that scores it, then a human review queue for high scores. The team tuned the classifier to its best-ever numbers, yet end-to-end miss rate barely moved.
q: 为什么单组件的提升没有传导到端到端指标？
q_en: Why did the single-component gain fail to reach the end-to-end metric?
options: 第一级没召回的内容分类器根本看不到，端到端上限被召回率卡住
分类模型和人审队列的通信协议不兼容，高分内容在中间队列被静默丢弃了
端到端指标本来就滞后于离线指标，再等几个训练周期它自己会追上来
人审队列的同事们对新模型给出的分数还不熟悉，需要一段适应期才会改变判断
options_en: Whatever stage one fails to retrieve never reaches the classifier, so recall at the first stage caps the whole pipeline.
The classifier and the review queue speak incompatible protocols, so high-scoring items are silently dropped in between.
End-to-end metrics simply lag offline ones, and after a few more training cycles they will catch up on their own.
The human reviewers are not used to the new model scores yet and need an adjustment period before their judgments change.
why: 多组件系统的端到端表现由级联决定：第一级漏掉的样本后面任何组件都救不回来，所以要先算每级的通过率再定优化顺序。代价是提高第一级召回会把更多噪声推给下游，分类和人审的负载都要跟着涨。
why_en: In a multi-stage pipeline the end-to-end number is a cascade: whatever stage one drops, no later stage can recover, and lifting stage-one recall pushes more noise and load onto everything downstream.

termDefinitions.meaning: 级联系统第一级从全量内容里筛出候选集的过程，决定了后续能看到什么。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Retrieval is the first stage that narrows all content down to a candidate set, deciding what later stages can ever see.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真正违规但系统没有拦下的比例，是审核系统的核心端到端指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Miss rate is the share of genuinely violating content the system fails to catch, the core end-to-end metric for moderation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个组件串联处理，整体表现是各级通过率的乘积。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cascade chains components in sequence, so overall performance is the product of each stage's pass-through rate.

optionExplanations: 级联的整体表现是各级相乘，任何一级的漏掉都是永久损失。
如果是协议丢消息，队列长度和投递量会对不上，这在监控里一眼能看出来。
端到端指标确实会滞后，但滞后只是延迟，不会凭空补上没被召回的样本。
人审适应期影响判定一致性，不影响那些压根没进队列的内容。
optionExplanations_en: A cascade multiplies stage rates, so anything dropped at one stage is a permanent loss downstream.
If the protocol were dropping messages, queue depth and delivery counts would disagree, which monitoring shows immediately.
End-to-end metrics do lag, but lag is only delay — it never recovers items that were never retrieved.
A reviewer adjustment period affects decision consistency, not content that never entered the queue at all.

scenario: 设计题接近尾声，面试官问：如果下周只能做一件事来改进这套推荐系统，你做什么？你已经在白板上列出了召回、排序、特征管线三处已知短板。
scenario_en: Near the end of the design, the interviewer asks: if you could do exactly one thing next week to improve this recommender, what would it be? You have already listed known weak spots in retrieval, ranking, and the feature pipeline.
q: 哪种回答最能体现实践经验这一评估信号？
q_en: Which answer best demonstrates the practical-experience signal?
options: 挑一处，说清它现在吃掉多少收益、为什么排在前面
把三处短板按重要程度全部讲一遍，让面试官自己从里面挑一个他最感兴趣的方向
回答会引入业界最新的模型架构，因为技术上更先进的方案通常能一次性解决多个问题
说需要先补齐完整的监控和数据看板，等指标都齐了再来判断哪一处最值得动手
options_en: Pick one, quantify the value it currently costs, and say why it ranks first.
Walk through all three weak spots in order of importance and let the interviewer choose whichever direction interests them most.
Say you would adopt the newest industry model architecture, since a technically more advanced approach usually fixes several problems at once.
Say you first need full monitoring and dashboards in place, and only once every metric exists can you judge which area deserves the work.
why: 这个问题考的是能不能在多个可改点里排出杠杆顺序并给出依据，而不是知识广度；代价是你必须承担排序判断的风险，说错了会被追问。
why_en: The question tests whether you can rank several candidate fixes by leverage and defend the ranking, not how many techniques you can list — and you own the risk of that call.
tradeoff: 定位单一最高杠杆点并给量化依据 vs 罗列全部候选改进把选择权推回给面试官
whenOtherWins: 如果系统真的还没有任何线上指标，先补基础监控确实是正确的第一步，但要说清楚要补哪几个指标。

termDefinitions.meaning: 同样的投入下能带来多大业务指标变化，用来给候选改进排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Leverage is how much business metric movement a fixed amount of work buys, used to rank candidate improvements.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推荐系统第一级，从海量物料里选出几百个候选交给排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Retrieval is a recommender's first stage, narrowing a huge catalog to a few hundred candidates for ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推荐系统第二级，对候选集精细打分并决定最终展示顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ranking is the second stage, scoring the candidate set precisely and deciding the final display order.

optionExplanations: 给出排序依据（损失多少收益）才叫经验判断，光说做哪个只是猜。
面试官问的就是你的优先级判断，把选择权交回去等于没有回答。
追新架构常见但风险高：不对着当前瓶颈动手，收益往往落不到线上。
监控是手段不是改进本身；系统已有已知短板时还等数据齐全会显得决断力不足。
optionExplanations_en: Naming what the gap currently costs is what makes it a judgment call rather than a guess.
The interviewer asked for your prioritization, so handing the choice back is a non-answer.
Chasing the newest architecture is common but risky: not aimed at the current bottleneck, the gain rarely lands in production.
Monitoring is a means, not the improvement; waiting for complete data when gaps are already known reads as indecision.

scenario: 给电商首页做商品推荐，可以形式化成「预测单个商品被点击的概率」的二分类，也可以形式化成需要成对偏好标注的 learning-to-rank。现有数据只有隐式点击日志，没有任何人工相关性标注，且预算不支持标注。
scenario_en: For homepage product recommendation you can frame it as binary classification predicting click probability, or as learning-to-rank needing pairwise preference labels. You only have implicit click logs, no human relevance annotations, and no budget to create them.
q: 按文章的论证角度，该选哪种形式化并用什么理由说服面试官？
q_en: Which formulation should you pick, and on what grounds should you defend it?
options: 选点击率二分类，理由是数据可得性：现有日志直接就是标签
选 learning-to-rank，理由是排序质量更贴近推荐这个业务目标，标注问题可以后面再想办法解决掉
选点击率二分类，理由是二分类模型的代码实现更简单，团队上手快且训练时间短很多
两种都实现出来做线上 A/B 对比，用真实业务数据来决定哪种形式化更适合这个场景
options_en: Pick click-probability classification, justified by data availability: the existing logs are already the labels.
Pick learning-to-rank, because ranking quality matches the business goal more closely, and the annotation problem can be solved somehow later on.
Pick click-probability classification, because binary models are simpler to implement, faster for the team to pick up, and much quicker to train.
Build both formulations and run an online A/B comparison, letting real business data decide which framing fits this scenario better.
why: 文章要求用业务影响、数据可得性、运营约束三个角度论证 formulation：这里数据可得性是决定性约束，成对偏好标签既不存在也买不起。代价是点击率模型只优化单品点击，位置偏差和列表整体多样性要靠后处理补。
why_en: Formulation choices are argued on business impact, data availability, and operational constraints — here availability decides, since pairwise labels neither exist nor fit the budget, and click models then need post-processing for position bias and diversity.
tradeoff: 数据可得性驱动的点击率二分类 vs 业务贴合度更高但依赖偏好标注的 learning-to-rank
whenOtherWins: 如果平台已经有大量成对偏好数据（例如搜索场景的人工相关性评级），learning-to-rank 直接优化列表顺序会更贴目标。

termDefinitions.meaning: Click-Through Rate（点击率）：曝光中被点击的比例，常作为推荐二分类模型的预测目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR stands for click-through rate, the share of impressions that get clicked, commonly the target of a binary recommendation model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 直接以列表排序质量为目标训练模型，通常需要成对或列表级的偏好标签。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Learning-to-rank trains directly against list ordering quality and usually needs pairwise or list-level preference labels.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个业务问题定义成哪一类 ML 任务（分类、排序、回归、预测）的选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Formulation is the choice of which ML task type — classification, ranking, regression, forecasting — a business problem becomes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排在前面的商品天然更容易被点击，使点击日志高估靠前位置的真实吸引力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Position bias means items shown higher get clicked more regardless of quality, so click logs overstate how appealing top slots really are.

optionExplanations: 三个论证角度里，这题被数据可得性一条卡死，其余两条都不改变结论。
业务贴合度确实更高，但标注既没预算也没时间，形式化不能建立在拿不到的数据上。
实现简单是团队便利，不是文章要求的三条论证角度之一，面试官不会认。
面试阶段就是要先论证选型；两条都实现的成本恰恰是运营约束不允许的。
optionExplanations_en: Of the three argument angles, data availability alone settles this one; the other two do not change the conclusion.
Business fit really is better, but there is no budget or time for labels, and a formulation cannot rest on data you cannot get.
Ease of implementation is team convenience, not one of the three justification angles the article asks for.
The interview asks you to argue the choice up front; building both is exactly what operational constraints rule out.
